scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on the CS LAB 1 PC (192.168.2.3) reports they cannot reach
the Server Room (1.0.0.x) or the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x). The
IT Department PCs are also affected. Other zones (Office, Principle,
Internet Lab itself) can still reach each other. What's wrong?
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router0 ripd daemon
Mechanism: router0 is the only L3 hop between IT Dept
  (192.168.1.0/24), CS Dept (192.168.2.0/24), and the rest
  of the network (reached via Serial2/0 to router1). When
  ripd dies on router0, router1 ages out the 192.168.1.0/24
  and 192.168.2.0/24 prefixes, and router0 itself stops
  learning the 1.0.0.0/8 / 128.168.0.0/16 / 192.168.3.0/24
  / 192.168.4.0/24 prefixes from router1. IT + CS PCs become
  isolated from everything beyond router0.
Localization: router0
Root cause: RIP routing daemon (ripd) not running on router0
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration on router0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ripd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router rip` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ripd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the rip configuration is missing/empty on router0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ripd daemon on router0 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
router0). Once ripd is running again it re-learns the remote prefixes and
re-advertises 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, restoring IT Dept and CS Dept
reachability.

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ripd back CONFIG-LESS and the rip service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ripd AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration (network statements) on router0. A proposal that restores the missing rip configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The RIP routing daemon (ripd) on router0 is completely absent: the FRR
daemons file has ripd=no and no /etc/frr/frr.conf exists on the device.
As a result, router0 has never participated in RIP and its routing table
contains only its three directly-connected subnets (192.168.1.0/24 —
IT LAN, 192.168.2.0/24 — CS LAN, and 10.0.0.0/8 — WAN link to
router1). When any CS or IT host sends traffic to the Server Room
(1.0.0.x) or Internet Lab (128.168.0.x), router0 has no matching route
and immediately returns ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" to the
sender — confirmed by live pings from cs_lab1. Office and Principle
zones are unaffected because they attach to router1, which does run RIP
and has a full table including routes learned from router2. The root
cause is that ripd was never enabled or configured on router0, leaving
it unable to learn or advertise any routes beyond its own segments.
The corrective fix is to create a valid /etc/frr/frr.conf on router0
containing a RIP stanza that enables ripd, sets the router-id, and
distributes the connected networks (192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24,
10.0.0.0/8) into RIP; change ripd=yes in /etc/frr/daemons; and
restart FRR (service frr restart). Once ripd exchanges updates with
router1, router0 will install routes to all remote subnets and CS/IT
traffic will flow normally.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names router0 as the affected device multiple times and attributes the ripd issue to router0.
Agent explicitly identifies the RIP daemon (ripd) / RIP routing as the affected component on router0.
The writeup explicitly states IT and CS hosts are isolated by router0 lacking RIP while Office/Principal zones via router1 remain unaffected, matching the expected symptom cluster.
Proposes enabling ripd in /etc/frr/daemons, creating the RIP config (network statements/router-id) on router0, and restarting FRR, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log directly shows ripd is not running, the daemons file disables ripd, frr.conf is missing, router0's routing table contains only connected routes, and pings from cs_lab1 fail with ICMP unreachable — the writeup's conclusions follow from these observations. The reasoning is complete and the recommended fix matches the observed misconfiguration.
